# flashrom

**Reads, writes and verifies SPI, LPC and parallel flash chips in place**

- **Version recorded:** 1.4.0
- **Categories:** `electronics`, `programmer`
- **Upstream:** <https://flashrom.org/>

## What it does

Talks directly to a flash chip — usually the SPI ROM holding a system's firmware — through a USB programmer or an on-board interface, and reads, erases, writes or verifies it.

## Why you would want it

It is how a firmware image gets off a board and back on again: dumping a router's ROM before modifying it, reflashing a bricked board through a clip, or recovering a system whose firmware update failed. For anyone working on RF hardware it is also the way into the flash on an SDR or a radio's control board.

## Before it will work

A programmer flashrom supports and, for in-circuit work, a way to hold the host CPU off the bus. Access comes from the `programmer` hardware class.

## How it installs

- apt: `flashrom`

## Known problems

The binary is `/usr/sbin/flashrom`, not `/usr/bin` — verified by listing the package contents on Debian 13 — so it is not on a normal user's PATH by default even after the group membership is right.

    Writing the wrong image to a system's boot flash produces a machine that
does not start, and recovering it needs the same programmer you already have. Read and keep a copy first; flashrom will do that in one command and it is the only step that cannot be redone afterwards.
